implementerProof.how: Drove the same surface independently, in a different container: the INFRA-69 tester container of the same Agent Sandbox issue pod, which has its own overlay (device 145 here against the implementer's 114), so the measurement is a second reading rather than a re-run in the same filesystem. /proc/mounts carries no /tmp line; stat puts /tmp, /home/legion, /home/legion/.cache and /home/legion/.local/state on one device (145) against /legion 149, /legion/feed 152, the sessions directory 165, /home/legion/.config 56 and /var/run/legion/{state,private,gh,launcher} 159/161/155/158; df -k --output=used / reads 13,640 KiB at rest, 218,440 KiB with a 200 MiB dd file under /tmp, under /home/legion/.cache and under $XDG_STATE_HOME (=/home/legion/.local/state/tester) alike, and 13,640 KiB again after each removal, while the same write under /legion, under /home/legion/.config and under the sessions directory left / at 13,640 KiB and grew those volumes (845,352 / 204,808 / 742,952 KiB). Every charged/not-charged claim of the implementer's proof reproduces. One parenthetical in that proof and in the note does not: see failure 1 — the proof's observation that `du -sx /` showed no change is correct, but its stated reason ('gVisor's overlay reports 0 blocks for such a file') is false, as `stat` and a direct `du` on the same file show.

failures.criterion: The note's cause is the measured one (spec acceptance 1): the note's own Evidence section states a false fact about this runtime, in the one note whose purpose is to correct a false fact.
failures.evidence: docs/solutions/testing/a-pod-harness-moves-tmpdir-too-and-the-failure-mode-is-a-silent-kill-INFRA-44.md:124-126 says '`du` reports 0 blocks for such a file on this gVisor overlay, so `df` on `/` is the instrument that sees the charge, not `du`'. Measured in the INFRA-69 tester container at head 78f0acf162ab7573ef5880b84649e9c2ef66d5b9 (the note byte-identical to the code head 62539c0449d752fdefe2fcafdd6a2f6d1c29b010): `dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/probe bs=1M count=200` then `stat -c 'blocks=%b' /tmp/probe` prints blocks=409600 (200 MiB in 512-byte blocks, not 0), `du -sk /tmp/probe` prints 204800 and `du -sk /tmp` prints 205614 — du pointed at the path sees the whole file. What is actually blind is a one-filesystem walk: `du -sx -k /` stays 42348 before and after the write, and `du -x -a -d1 -k /` prints `0\t/tmp`, because the written file reports `dev=143` while its parent directory reports `dev=145` (`stat -c '%n dev=%d' /tmp /tmp/probe /home/legion/.cache /home/legion/.cache/probe/f` → /tmp dev=145, /tmp/probe dev=143, /home/legion/.cache dev=145, its file dev=143), so `du -x` skips every written file as being on another device — from /home too (`du -sx -k /home` = 13516 unchanged with 200 MiB under ~/.cache), not only from /. Consequence for a reader: the note tells them du cannot see their usage, when `du -sh ~/.cache` is exactly the instrument that finds the 4.4 GiB of Go caches the note quotes 15 lines above from dispatch://INFRA-51. Fix: say that a `du` walk with `-x` misses these files because a written file reports a different device than its parent on this gVisor overlay, that `du` without `-x` (or pointed at the directory) reports them correctly, and that `df -k --output=used /` is what measures the whole container filesystem. The same parenthetical is in the PR body's `E2E (implementer)` line and must be corrected there too. No repository test pins this: the repository has no checker over docs/solutions/ prose (`.github/workflows/docs.yaml` filters on docs/site/**, packages/**, skills/** and two scripts; `.github/scripts/check-private-names.sh` only forbids private names), and a Bun test grepping the note for a sentence would be a source-text test the repository's conventions forbid and that would be deleted by the fix. The red evidence is the command above, which anyone can re-run in a role container.

failures.criterion: A reader can tell from the note which directories are charged and which are not (spec acceptance 2): two of the five paths the not-charged list calls 'in-memory directories' are not emptyDirs and cannot be written at all.
failures.evidence: The note's line 50-51 reads 'the in-memory directories /home/legion/.config, /var/run/legion/private, /var/run/legion/state, /var/run/legion/launcher and /var/run/legion/gh'. In the golden pod JSON the implementer cites, only `config`, `private-<role>` and `state-<role>` are `emptyDir: {medium: Memory}`; `launcher-<role>` and `gh-<role>` are Secret volumes (packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/testdata/golden/root.json). Live in the tester container they are read-only 9p mounts, not tmpfs: `grep -E ' /run/legion/(launcher|gh|private|state) ' /proc/mounts` shows `9p ro` for gh and launcher against `tmpfs rw` for state and private, and `touch /var/run/legion/launcher/.probe` and `touch /var/run/legion/gh/.probe` both fail read-only while the same touch under private and state succeeds. The not-charged verdict is right for all five; the description is wrong for two, and a reader told a read-only Secret mount is an in-memory scratch directory may try to put a cache there. Fix: name the three in-memory emptyDirs as such and the two Secret mounts as read-only credential mounts a reader cannot write to.

failures.criterion: The note reads as finished prose (the artifact of this change is its text): one sentence is ungrammatical.
failures.evidence: Line 60-61: 'A habit of "put the big download in /tmp" is evicted for here; nothing about `/tmp` in a role container is free.' 'is evicted for here' is not a sentence. Fix the clause (for example 'A habit of "put the big download in /tmp" gets the pod evicted here').

Devices: /tmp, /home/legion, /home/legion/.cache and /home/legion/.local/state all 145; /legion 149; /legion/feed 152; sessions 165; /home/legion/.config 56; /var/run/legion/state 159, private 161, gh 155, launcher 158. df on / : 13,640 KiB at rest; 218,440 KiB with the file under /tmp, the same 218,440 KiB under /home/legion/.cache and the same again under $XDG_STATE_HOME (=/home/legion/.local/state/tester, so Oh My Pi's state home is charged as the note says); 13,640 KiB again after every removal. TMPDIR is unset in this container, which is the premise of the note's fourth-variable bullet.
proof.negativeControl: The same write under /legion left / at 13,640 KiB and took /legion's used figure to 845,352 KiB; under /home/legion/.config it left / unchanged and grew that tmpfs to 204,808 KiB; under the sessions directory it left / unchanged and grew the issue volume to 742,952 KiB. The instrument therefore tells a volume-backed or memory-backed path from a charged one, and would have shown /tmp as uncharged had /tmp been the memory-backed mount the superseded cluster read called it.
